title: Mass tourism or ecotourism: which is better for a place?

figure.name: x-compare
figure.verdict: Tourism helps most when locals benefit and nature is protected

explain.say: Imagine your town is so beautiful that millions of visitors arrive every year. Is that good news or bad news? Look at the board. Here are two kinds of tourism, which means travelling for fun: mass tourism on the left, ecotourism on the right.

draw.text: Mass tourism or ecotourism: which is better for a place?

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: Tourism helps most when locals benefit and nature is protected

explain.say: Look at mass tourism: huge numbers of visitors, big hotels and cruise ships. Venice in Italy has only about 50,000 people living in its old centre, but millions of visitors a year. In 2024 it began charging day visitors on busy days. Can you guess what problems crowds bring?

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: Tourism helps most when locals benefit and nature is protected

explain.say: Mass tourism brings jobs, but much of the money can leave the area, going to big hotel chains and airlines from abroad. That is called leakage. Crowds also bring litter, traffic and higher rents for local people. Have you ever been somewhere very crowded?

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: Tourism helps most when locals benefit and nature is protected

explain.say: Now ecotourism: small groups, local guides and caring for nature. Costa Rica protects about a quarter of its land in parks and reserves, and visitors pay to see sloths, turtles and rainforest. That gives local people a reason to protect the forest. Can you see how nature becomes worth more alive?

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: Tourism helps most when locals benefit and nature is protected

explain.say: Kenya’s wildlife parks, Bhutan’s visitor fee and Rwanda’s gorilla treks all try to make tourism help nature and local people. Great thinking! Challenge: plan a holiday that would help the people and nature of the place you visit.

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: Tourism helps most when locals benefit and nature is protected

faq.a: Mass tourism is when very large numbers of tourists visit the same places, often on package holidays, in big resorts or on cruise ships. Too many visitors is sometimes called overtourism.
Ecotourism is responsible travel to natural places that protects the environment and helps local people, usually in small groups with local guides.
Leakage is when money spent by tourists flows out of the local area, for example to foreign-owned hotels, airlines and imported food, instead of staying with local people.
Venice is so crowded that local people find it hard to live there. In 2024 it started charging day visitors a fee on busy days, to spread out the crowds and pay for looking after the city.

faq.q: How does tourism help protect gorillas in Rwanda?
faq.a: Visitors pay a high fee for a permit to trek to see mountain gorillas. The money pays rangers to protect the park, and part of it goes to nearby villages, so local people benefit from keeping gorillas safe.

facts: In 2024 Venice began charging day visitors an entry fee on busy days.
Costa Rica protects about a quarter of its land in national parks and reserves.
Rwanda charges US$1,500 for a permit to trek to see mountain gorillas.
